No, calibration is not the primary cause of variation in liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) testosterone measurement. While calibration is an essential step in the process, variations in LC-MS/MS testosterone measurement are more likely due to other factors such as:

1. Ion suppression or enhancement
2. Matrix effects
3. Instrumental variability
4. Sample preparation and extraction methods
5. Interference from other compounds

Proper calibration can help minimize some of these variations, but it is not the sole cause of variation in LC-MS/MS testosterone measurement.
